brief: Fed, ECB and BoJ have all hiked in the past two weeks, restarting a globally synchronised tightening cycle markets are still pricing further into. DB argues investors risk underestimating its eventual scale for four reasons. First, rising commodity prices (Brent near $102/bbl, the Bloomberg Commodity Spot Index above June-August levels) have not yet fed through to inflation data or surveys, and energy shocks tend to produce second-round effects. Second, central banks are overcorrecting for being seen as too slow in 2021-23, hiking now with inflation below half the 8%+ level that triggered 2022 hikes. Fed Chair Warsh has flagged over five years of above-target inflation. Third, financial conditions are looser than in 2022: the S&P 500 is near record highs, US high-yield spreads are around 270bps versus above 400bps then, and euro high-yield spreads are under half their 2022 level, meaning less of the tightening burden is being done for central banks. Fourth, markets have historically underpriced every major Fed and ECB hiking cycle since 1994. DB concludes that risk-asset resilience, itself a product of growth strength since the Iran conflict began, signals central banks have room to hike further, not that the cycle is nearly done.
